I am a 50-year-old farmer in Quzhou County with no schooling. I have farmed my whole life, and I know my land. I have about 10 mu of fields. My wheat is already in the ground — I sowed it last October after the holiday, and now in April it is growing green and strong. I will harvest it in early June, and then right away I will plant maize on that same land. This wheat-maize rotation is what my father did, and it is what everyone in my village does. It is safe and we know it well. I buy improved wheat seeds and hybrid maize seeds from the county shop. For wheat, I till the soil with the rotary machine before sowing. For maize, I do not till — I plant the seeds directly into the wheat stubble after harvest, which saves time and fuel.

This year I will also plant about 2 mu of cotton in April. The cotton price was okay last year, and my wife and I can pick it together in autumn. We need this cash for family expenses. The cotton needs more work — many sprays for insects — but 2 mu is not too much for us to manage. I will till the cotton field with the rotary machine.

For the wheat, I will irrigate four times and spray pesticides four times. For the maize, I will irrigate three times and spray three times. The cotton will need about three irrigations and many pesticide sprays to keep the bollworms away. I use the fertilizers the same way I have always done — not too much, just enough.
